audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Benjamin and Saul genealogies, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for differences from chapter 7, family relocation, wives and divorce/sending away, Moab residence, builders and towns, expulsion from Gath, Jerusalem residence, Saul/Jonathan names, Baal-name reception, disability-related name alteration, archers, and fertility hierarchy.

verses.restored: Benjamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Ashbel second, Aharah third,
Nohah fourth, and Rapha fifth.
Sons of Bela: Addar, Gera, Abihud,
Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,
Gera, Shephuphan, and Huram.
These were sons of Ehud, heads of ancestral houses of inhabitants of Geba, who were relocated to Manahath:
Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera; he relocated them and fathered Uzza and Ahihud.
Shaharaim fathered children in field/land of Moab after sending away Hushim and Baara his wives.
By Hodesh his wife he fathered Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,
Jeuz, Sachia, and Mirmah. These were his sons, heads of ancestral houses.
By Hushim he fathered Abitub and Elpaal.
Sons of Elpaal: Eber, Misham, and Shemed, who built Ono and Lod with their towns;
also Beriah and Shema, heads of ancestral houses of inhabitants of Aijalon, who drove away inhabitants of Gath.
Ahio, Shashak, Jeremoth,
Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,
Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were sons of Beriah.
Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,
Ishmerai, Izliah, and Jobab were sons of Elpaal.
Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,
Elienai, Zillethai, Eliel,
Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were sons of Shimei.
Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,
Abdon, Zichri, Hanan,
Hananiah, Elam, Anthothijah,
Iphdeiah and Penuel were sons of Shashak.
Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,
Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri were sons of Jeroham.
These were heads of ancestral houses according to generations, chief men; these lived in Jerusalem.
At Gibeon lived Jeiel father/founder of Gibeon; name of his wife was Maacah.
His firstborn son Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,
Gedor, Ahio, and Zecher/Zechariah.
Mikloth fathered Shimeah. They also lived with their brothers in Jerusalem, opposite their brothers.
Ner fathered Kish; Kish fathered Saul; Saul fathered Jonathan, Malchi-shua, Abinadab, and Esh-baal.
Son of Jonathan was Merib-baal; Merib-baal fathered Micah.
Sons of Micah: Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.
Ahaz fathered Jehoaddah; Jehoaddah fathered Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri; Zimri fathered Moza;
Moza fathered Binea; Raphah was his son, Eleasah his son, Azel his son.
Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All these were sons of Azel.
Sons of Eshek his brother: Ulam firstborn, Jeush second, Eliphelet third.
Sons of Ulam were mighty warriors and archers, with many sons and grandsons—one hundred fifty. All these were descendants of Benjamin.

translation_notes: This Benjamin genealogy differs from chapter 7 and other biblical lists; it is a constructed archive, not a seamless modern family tree.
Verses 6-7 describe relocation whose agency and coercion are unclear; displaced families should not be treated as administrative objects.
Shaharaim sends away wives Hushim and Baara. The text gives no consent, economic, custody, or survival details for the women.
Living in Moab and interregional marriage undermine ethnic-purity readings.
Ono and Lod are built by named descendants, preserving civic labor within genealogy.
Driving out inhabitants of Gath is displacement and must not be celebrated merely as ancestral expansion.
Esh-baal and Merib-baal preserve names containing Baal; later forms Ish-bosheth and Mephibosheth may reflect scribal substitution. Baal-name elements do not prove moral corruption.
Merib-baal/Mephibosheth's disability story in Samuel must not be erased or stigmatized by name changes.
Military ability, archery, and number of sons are not measures of masculine or family worth.
safety_note: Do not use Benjamin's genealogy to justify ethnic purity, forced relocation, abandonment of wives, expulsion of residents, disability stigma, or militarized masculinity. Preserve textual differences and the humanity of people moved, sent away, or driven out.
